title.value: Augmenting Human Selves Through Artificial Agents – Lessons From the Brain
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: Augmenting Human Selves Through Artificial Agents – Lessons From the Brain

extractions.description: This paper explores how artificial intelligence (AI) can augment human capabilities, such as wellbeing and morality, by focusing on the brain's 'environment-agent nexus.' It proposes integrating the free energy principle (FEP) with the dynamic temporo-spatial view of neuro-mental processes to create adaptive AI agents. Potential applications range from psychiatric self-regulation to environmental disaster prediction.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper does not focus on sustainable development as a central theme, but rather on augmenting human intelligence and decision-making through AI, drawing inspiration from the brain's adaptive capacities.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Much of current artificial intelligence (AI) and the drive toward artificial general intelligence (AGI) focuses on developing machines for functional tasks that humans accomplish...In this paper, we focus on how a machine can augment humans rather than do what they do, and we extend this beyond AGI-style tasks to augmenting peculiarly personal human capacities, such as wellbeing and morality.

primary_category.justification: The paper mentions the use of AI for environmental disaster prediction, which falls under Climate Science, specifically extreme weather event prediction.
primary_category.quote: Especially in the age of climate change, we require tools to properly predict such environmental crises well ahead of time in a more fine-grained way.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper discusses predicting environmental disasters such as wildfires, which aligns with climate modeling and predictions.
primary_sub_category.quote: Especially in the age of climate change, we require tools to properly predict such environmental crises well ahead of time in a more fine-grained way... Wildfire prediction could thus incorporate these variables over a long temporal range that, as such, is not accessible to humans.

applications.value: Extreme weather detection and tracking (locally and globally)
applications.justification: The paper explicitly mentions using AI to predict environmental crises like wildfires.
